election_dates.primarySnippet: 25 P.S. § 2753(a): There shall be a General primary preceding each general election which shall be held on the third Tuesday of May in all even-numbered years, except in the year of the nomination of a President of the United States, in which year the General primary shall be held on the fourth Tuesday of April.
election_dates.generalSnippet: Pa. Const. art. VII, § 2 (General Election Day): The general election shall be held biennially on the Tuesday next following the first Monday of November in each even-numbered year, but the General Assembly may by law fix a different day, two-thirds of all the members of each House consenting thereto: Provided, That such election shall always be held in an even-numbered year.

state_background_check.value: No — Pennsylvania's constitution bars anyone convicted of embezzlement of public moneys, bribery, perjury, or other infamous crime from the General Assembly or from holding any office of trust or profit in the Commonwealth, but the U.S. Constitution's own qualifications for Congress (age, citizenship, residency) can't be added to by any state, so this doesn't reach U.S. House or Senate candidates
state_background_check.snippet: Pa. Const. art. II, § 7: "No person hereafter convicted of embezzlement of public moneys, bribery, perjury or other infamous crime, shall be eligible to the General Assembly, or capable of holding any office of trust or profit in this Commonwealth." Congressional qualifications are set exclusively by the U.S. Constitution, confirmed per https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R41946.html: "the Framers intended the Constitution to be the exclusive source of qualifications for Members of Congress, and that the Framers thereby 'divested' States of any power to add qualifications."

bio_summary.value: A fifth-generation Northeastern Pennsylvanian, Rob Bresnahan is a husband, businessman, and community leader. As a 19 year-old, Rob took the reins of his grandfather’s union electrical contracting company and expanded the business across the Commonwealth while tripling the number of good-paying union jobs. He dedicated his career to revitalizing our community, helping local entrepreneurs, and creating jobs for Pennsylvania families.

civic_affiliations.snippet: Cognetti was appointed to the Scranton School Board in 2017, [ 8 ] but resigned in December 2018 to become a special assistant to Pennsylvania's state auditor, Eugene DePasquale . [ 9 ] While serving on the board, she criticized no-bid school bus contracts and unapproved payments to contractors. [ 10 ] Mayor of Scranton [ edit ] Elections [ edit ] Cognetti ran in the 2019 special election to finish the term of Scranton mayor Bill Courtright , who had pleaded guilty to corruption charges earlier that year. [ 11 ] She ran as an independent after she deemed the local Democratic Party's closed caucus system undemocratic. Her campaign emphasized investments in local businesses, education, and infrastructure. [ 12 ] She won the special election with 36% of the vote. [ 3 ] In 2021, Cognetti ran as a Democrat for a full term and defeated her Republican opponent, 72.5% to 23.4%. [ 13 ] [ 14 ] Tenure [ edit ] During Cognetti's tenure as mayor, Scranton completed its exit from Pennsylvania's Act 47 financial distress program and improved its bond rating, allowing the city to reduce reliance on short-term borrowing. [ 15 ] Her administration undertook infrastructure and public works projects, including investments in stormwater systems and parks, demolition of hazardous structures, and upgrades to municipal signage. [ 15 ] The city's housing stock expanded, while the administration implemented initiatives to modernize municipal operations and improve service efficiency. [ 16 ] Downtown redevelopment also continued during this period, accompanied by increased construction activity across the city. [ 16 ] In 2024, President Joe Biden appointed Cognetti to the United States Trade Representative 's Advisory Committee for Trade Policy and Negotiations.

bio_summary.value: Paige Cognetti (née Gebhardt ; born August 27, 1980) [ 1 ] is an American politician serving since 2020 as mayor of Scranton , Pennsylvania . She is the first woman to be mayor of the city and won her seat in a special election. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] A member of the Democratic Party, she ran her first Scranton mayoral campaign as an Independent. She is the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania's 8th congressional district in 2026. [ 4 ]
